title: Isomorphism and structural invariants
section: Part B: Abstract Algebra ▷ The Concept of Isomorphism
terms: isomorphism; isomorphic groups; structural invariant; nonisomorphic groups.

exposition.text:
A group isomorphism is a bijection f : G → H satisfying f (ab) = f(a)f(b). It transfers
the entire group structure, including identity, inverses, element orders, subgroup structure,
commutativity, and cyclicity. Names of elements and symbols for operations are irrelevant.
To disprove isomorphism, find one differing invariant; equal order alone is far from sufficient. To
prove isomorphism, give a well-defined bijective operation-preserving map, or apply a classifi-

question.text:
Which group is isomorphic to the multiplicative group {1, −1, i, −i}?
∗
(A) Z × Z (B) Z (C) S (D) (Z, +) (E) (Z/8Z)
2 2 4 3

solution.text:
The element i has order four and generates the group. Therefore it is cyclic of order four
and isomorphic to Z ; both other groups of order four listed have exponent two.

Which property distinguishes (Q, +) from (Q , ·) and therefore proves that they are not iso-

(A) Only the first is countable
(B) Only the first is Abelian
(C) Only the first admits a group square root of every element
(D) Only the first has an identity
(E) Only the first is infinite

solution.text:
In additive notation the first group is divisible by two: x = a/2 solves x + x = a. The
2
analogous multiplicative equation x = a in positive rationals has no rational solution at
a = 2. Here a group square root means an element whose product with itself, under the
specified group operation, is the given element.

question.text:
Which group is isomorphic to Z ?
12
(A) Z × Z
3 4
(B) Z × Z
2 6
(C) Z × Z × Z
2 2 3
(D) S × Z
3 2
(E) The alternating group A
4

solution.text:
Because 3 and 4 are coprime, (1, 1) has order twelve in the first product. The other abelian
products have no element of order twelve, and the nonabelian groups cannot be cyclic.

question.text:
Which invariant distinguishes Z × Z from Z × Z ?
8 2 4 4
(A) The number of identity elements
(B) Commutativity
(C) Whether the group is finite
(D) The largest element order
(E) Group order

solution.text:
The first group contains an element of order eight, while every element of the second has
order dividing four. Isomorphisms preserve element orders.
